decided_at_provenance: Captured from date -u immediately before writing; the owner answered the AskUserQuestion immediately prior.
context: The sibling audit mandated by the eof-after-closed decision (protected/us017-eof-after-closed-owner-decision-2026-08-28.json, sha bd7849c3) found the same defect shape on two further driver paths, both gated on terminal_delivered. (1) DriverInput::Inbound after Terminal delivery: no branch runs, so poll() returns the initial InputDisposition::Consumed{bytes:N} while the core never sees the bytes. Measured empirically with a scratch probe: Consumed{bytes:7} with counts.input_bytes 0 before and 0 after. This is WORSE than the EOF defect, which merely absorbed an input silently — this one absorbs it AND reports success, so a correct adapter cannot detect the loss, and none of the three fail-closed driver codes would catch it. (2) Producer commands after Terminal: TerminalRejected without a core call, where the oracle reports STATE_VIOLATION. Both are unreachable in the public corpus today, so neither masks a current result.

decisions.decision: SAME RULING AS THE EOF DEFECT — PASS IT THROUGH. The bytes must reach the core so its typed refusal is surfaced. The owner's stated reasoning extends directly and with more force: absorbing an event the reference implementation reports is a real behavioural change, and reporting success for work never done is strictly worse than silence because it defeats detection.

MAKE IT CONSISTENT — apply the same principle so every post-terminal path behaves alike. This path at least reports a refusal rather than false success, so it is less severe, but leaving two post-terminal paths on different principles is how the next sibling hides.

constraints: The public corpus must stay 74/74 with the transcript byte-identical modulo the runtime object, and scored-field disagreements with live Java must remain zero.

Any driver-side detection mechanism that would require the adapter to read core counters around a poll edges toward adapter-side protocol logic and needs its own owner decision; do not add one silently.
If either fix makes any of the three fail-closed driver codes reachable, say so and test them against a real occurrence.
